snippet.title: Hutspiel - (1955)
snippet.description:
Name: Hutspiel
Developer: Dorothy K. Clark, Archie N. Colby, Paul Iribe, Nicholas M. Smith, Lloy D. Yates
Year: 1955
Simulation Not Available. 2 player. 
Platform: GEDA

Hutspiel is one of the first complex computer games, a military wargame for the Goodyear Electronic Differential Analyzer (GEDA) that simulates at a theatre level. Its intention was to study the use of tactical nuclear weapons and conventional air support in Western Europe in the event of a Soviet invasion.
The game pits two players against each other with one controlling NATO forces in France, Belgium and West Germany, and the other in control of a Soviet invasion force trying to penetrate a 150 mile frontage. Players could allocate forces across sectors of the map and set targets (such as airfields, enemy troops, supply depots and transportation facilities) for planes and nukes.
Interestingly, the report notes that players usually didn't play the game confrontationally. Instead, each side would agree on a strategy in advance, and play to find out what happened! (Remember, this was a research project.
Comment: a complex game, more military oriented.


There´s no playable version, sorry :(

More info here:
https://if50.substack.com/p/hutspiel-and-dr-dorothy-k-clark
Song:
Lights - Patrick Patrikios
